definition_zh: 认证；正式认可；委派；归功于
definition_en: to officially approve an institution or course, to send an official with credentials, or to credit someone with something
core_image: 一份盖了章的证书，证明某机构或某人够格
scene: 工程系等了两年的评审，专家组走访实验室后终于出具认可文件。The programme was accredited by the national board.
sceneCN: 这里 accredit 是「认证、正式认可」（第 1 个义项：官方认定某机构或课程合格）；句意为该项目获得国家委员会的认证。

pos.zh: 认证；正式认可；委派；把……归功于

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「认证；资格认定」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「获认证的；被委派的」

senses.title: To certify officially
senses.definition: to declare officially that an institution, course, or person meets a standard
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某机构、课程或人员达到标准
senses.example: The laboratory is accredited to run these tests.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验室获准开展这些检测。
senses.why: Latin credere means 'to trust'; to accredit is to give credit, to declare that something can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为「信任」；accredit 就是给予信任，宣布某物可以被信赖。

senses.title: To send with credentials
senses.definition: to appoint an ambassador or journalist officially to a post or place
senses.definitionCN: 正式任命大使或记者到某职位或某地
senses.example: The paper accredited two reporters to the peace talks.
senses.exampleCN: 该报派了两名记者获准采访和平谈判。
senses.why: Credentials are letters of trust; sending someone accredited means sending a person the host agrees to trust.
senses.whyCN: credentials 是信任文书；派人「获认证」意味着所派之人是东道主同意信任的。

senses.title: To attribute credit to someone
senses.definition: to give someone the credit for an achievement or a discovery
senses.definitionCN: 把某项成就或发现的功劳给予某人
senses.example: The invention is usually accredited to a Swiss engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发明通常被归功于一位瑞士工程师。
senses.why: Here the gift of trust becomes the gift of credit: the name that gets attached to a result.
senses.whyCN: 这里给予信任变成给予功劳：那个被附在成果上的名字。

intro.en: Accredit pairs the Latin prefix ad- with credit, from credere, 'to trust'.
intro.cn: accredit 把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与 credit 结合，credit 源自 credere（信任）。

items.en: credere meant 'to trust, believe', the root of creed and credible.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、相信」，是 creed 与 credible 的词根。

items.en: creditum meant 'something entrusted, a loan'.
items.cn: creditum 意为「所托付之物、贷款」。

items.en: French credit carried both trust and financial credit.
items.cn: 法语 credit 兼指信任与金融信用。

items.en: English formed accredit to mean 'give credit or authority to'.
items.cn: 英语构成 accredit，意为「给予信用或授权」。

items.en: The verb came to name the sending of an accredited envoy.
items.cn: 这个动词后来指派出获认可使节。

items.en: Modern usage centres on institutional certification and attribution.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在机构认证与功劳归属。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and participle plus credit words; the second gathers verbs of official approval.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、分词与 credit 相关词；第二组收表示官方认可的动词。

entries.definition: The official recognition given to an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「认证」，给予机构的正式认可。

entries.definition: An adjective for an approved school, lab, or reporter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「获认证的、被委派的」。

entries.definition: A document proving trust or qualification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「资格证书」，证明信任或资格的文件。

entries.definition: Trust, praise, or a financial arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信用、功劳、赊账」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to confirm officially in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明、认证」，以书面正式确认。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to give official power to act.
A verb meaning to grant official permission.
A verb meaning to name the cause or author.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the credit root and the board phrases; the abstract hooks picture a stamped certificate handed over.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 credit 词根与委员会搭配；抽象记忆点想象盖了章的证书被递交。

normal.en: Accredit is 'give credit': credere means to trust.
normal.cn: accredit 是「给予信用」：credere 意为信任。

normal.en: Be accredited by is the standard passive pattern.
normal.cn: be accredited by 是标准被动结构。

normal.en: An accredited representative is an officially accepted envoy.
normal.cn: accredited representative 指被正式接受的代表。

normal.en: Accredit someone with an invention means to credit them.
normal.cn: accredit someone with an invention 意为把发明归功于他。

normal.en: The noun is accreditation, common in education and hospitals.
normal.cn: 名词是 accreditation，常用于教育界与医院。

abstract.en: Picture a board stamping a certificate on a dean's desk.
abstract.cn: 想象委员会在院长桌上盖章认证。

abstract.en: Picture a reporter handed a pass at a summit door.
abstract.cn: 想象记者在峰会门口领到通行证。

abstract.en: Picture a museum label naming one engineer beneath a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象机器下方的博物馆标签写着一个工程师的名字。

examples.en: The college is accredited by the regional board.
examples.cn: 这所学院获得地区委员会认证。

examples.en: Only accredited journalists may enter the hall.
examples.cn: 只有获准采访的记者才能进入大厅。

examples.en: The discovery is often accredited to a team in Berlin.
examples.cn: 这项发现常被归功于柏林的一个团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克莱迪特」——把信任盖章给对方，就是认证与委派。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ credere（信任）→ credit；核心义是「把信任正式给予某人或某机构」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from certifying an institution, to sending an accepted representative, to crediting a person with a result.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从认证机构，走到派出被接受的代表，再到把成果归于某人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped paper that says 'trusted'
core.cn: 核心意象：盖了章、写着「可信」的纸

branches.en: Official recognition that a standard is met.
branches.cn: 达到标准的正式认可。

branches.en: An envoy sent with letters of trust.
branches.cn: 带信任文书派出的代表。

branches.en: The name attached to an achievement.
branches.cn: 附在成就上的名字。

branches.en: Both senses hand out trust in a formal form.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以正式形式发出信任。

branches.en: Certifying and crediting both assign standing.
branches.cn: 认证与归功都在分配地位。

intro.en: The word joins the Latin prefix ad- with the trust root cred-, and its family adds the action and participle forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与「信任」词根 cred- 结合，词族另加动作与分词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin credere and creditum are the ancestors, so the Latin entries record the verb and the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 credere 与 creditum 是祖先，因此拉丁条目记录动词与名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「认证；资格认定」
形容词，义为「获认证的；被委派的」

definition_en: to collect or increase in quantity gradually over a period of time
core_image: 雪球顺着斜坡滚下，一路把新雪粘到身上
scene: 老屋已经很久没人住了，琴盖上落了厚厚一层灰。Dust had accumulated on the old piano.
sceneCN: 这里的 accumulate 是「堆积」（第 2 个义项：东西一点点堆在一处）；句意是旧钢琴上积了一层灰。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「累积的」
由词干加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「蓄能器；累加器」

senses.title: To build up something valuable
senses.definition: to gather more and more of something useful or valuable over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移，把有用的或有价值的东西越聚越多
senses.example: She accumulated a large collection of rare books.
senses.exampleCN: 她积累了一大批珍本书。
senses.why: The Latin noun cumulus names a heap, and ad- points things towards it, so the verb pictures valuables being heaped into one store.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 cumulus 指「堆」，前缀 ad- 表示「朝着一处」，所以这个词画出的是把有价值的东西往同一个仓里堆。

senses.title: To pile up in one place
senses.definition: to collect in a growing pile, usually without anyone arranging it
senses.definitionCN: 东西无人整理地越堆越多，聚在一处
senses.example: Snow accumulated against the garden wall.
senses.exampleCN: 雪在院墙边越积越高。
senses.why: The same heap image turns literal: snow, dust and papers have no owner adding them, yet they still form a cumulus.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「堆」的意象在这里变成实景：雪、灰和纸张并没有人刻意去添，却照样堆成一个土丘似的形状。

senses.title: To grow in intensity
senses.definition: to increase gradually until a feeling or problem becomes strong
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或问题逐渐加重，直到变得强烈
senses.example: Tension accumulated between the two neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 两个邻居之间的紧张情绪越积越重。
senses.why: A heap can be made of feelings as well as objects; each small grievance adds one more layer until the mass presses down.
senses.whyCN: 堆起来的不只是实物，也可以是情绪；每一次小小的不满都加一层，最后整堆重量压了下来。

intro.en: The word is Latin in both parts: a prefix of direction and a noun for a heap.
intro.cn: 这个词的两半都来自拉丁语：一个表示方向的前缀，一个表示「堆」的名词。

items.en: cumulus meant a heap, a mass or a pile.
items.cn: cumulus 意为堆、团、垛。

items.en: accumulare joined ad-, towards, with cumulus, to heap something up.
items.cn: accumulare 把表示「朝向」的 ad- 与 cumulus 结合，意为把东西堆起来。

items.en: the participle accumulatus described what had been piled together.
items.cn: 分词 accumulatus 描述已经堆在一起的东西。

items.en: accumulate entered English as a learned verb of heaping and adding.
items.cn: accumulate 在十五世纪进入英语，是书面语中表示「堆叠、添加」的动词。

items.en: it now covers money, data, experience, dust and even stress.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖金钱、数据、经验、灰尘，甚至压力。

note.en: The first group is the cumulus family; the second is other verbs of collecting.
note.cn: 第一组是 cumulus 词族；第二组是别的表示收集的动词。

entries.definition: the process or result of heaping things up
tending to grow by repeated addition
a device that stores energy or numbers
increasing by successive additions
to collect a large amount of something
to bring things together in one place
to form a heap through repeated addition
to bring items together as a set

normalIntro.en: These hints follow cumulus, the Latin heap at the centre of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条都围绕词心的拉丁语 cumulus（堆）。

normal.en: cumulus is Latin for a heap, and it also gives us the cloud name.
normal.cn: cumulus 是拉丁语的「堆」，积云的名字也来自它。

normal.en: ad- means towards, so the verb is literally to heap towards one point.
normal.cn: ad- 意为「朝向」，所以这个词字面上就是往一点上堆。

normal.en: -ate marks the Latin verb, parallel to calculate and estimate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标记拉丁动词，与 calculate、estimate 同一套路。

normal.en: accumulation is the noun, and accumulative describes the growing kind.
normal.cn: accumulation 是名词，accumulative 形容「越积越多」的那一类。

normal.en: the verb keeps company with wealth, knowledge, evidence and dust.
normal.cn: 这个词常与财富、知识、证据、灰尘这些宾语同现。

abstract.en: Watch a snowball roll downhill and swell with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象雪球滚下坡，每转一圈就胖一圈。

abstract.en: Picture coins dropping into a glass jar until it is full.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币一枚枚落进玻璃罐，直到装满。

abstract.en: See layers of dust settle on a forgotten piano.
abstract.cn: 想象灰尘一层层落在一架被遗忘的钢琴上。

examples.en: Small savings accumulate quickly if you add to them each month.
examples.cn: 如果每月都添一点，小笔储蓄很快就会累积起来。

examples.en: Letters accumulated on the desk while she was away.
examples.cn: 她外出期间，桌上的信越堆越多。

examples.en: He accumulated enough evidence to prove his case.
examples.cn: 他收集到了足以证明自己主张的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿丘缪累特」——阿丘把东西一件件往怀里搂，越搂越沉，累得直喘。

root: 拉丁语 accumulare（堆起来），由 ad-（朝向）与 cumulus（堆）构成；本义是把东西往一处堆，后引申为数量逐渐增多。

sensesIntro.en: One heap image serves three scales: valuables stored up, objects piling on their own, and feelings pressing down.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「堆」的意象管着三种尺度：存起来的值钱物、自己堆高的实物、以及压下来的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap that grows layer by layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层一层长高的堆。

branches.en: money, books and knowledge stored up on purpose
branches.cn: 有意存起来的钱、书与知识

branches.en: snow, dust and paper gathering without a keeper
branches.cn: 无人照看而自行堆积的雪、灰与纸张

branches.en: grievances and tension adding weight
branches.cn: 不断加重的不满与紧张

branches.en: invisible things that still behave like a heap
branches.cn: 虽无形却仍像堆一样增长的东西

branches.en: quantity rising whether or not someone intends it
branches.cn: 不管有意无意，数量都在往上走

intro.en: A Latin prefix, a Latin noun and a verb ending make the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁名词和一个动词词尾，拼成了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The heap root cumulus also appears in cumulative and in the cloud name cumulus.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「堆」的词根 cumulus 也出现在 cumulative 和云名 cumulus 里。

definition_en: a statement saying that someone has done something wrong
core_image: 一根手指直直指向对面的人
scene: 他声音平静，否认了那项指控。He denied the accusation with a calm voice.
sceneCN: 这里的 accusation 是「指控」（第 1 个义项：正式说某人有错）；句意是他平静地否认了指控。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「指控；指责」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「被指控的」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「指控者」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「指责的」

senses.title: A formal charge against someone
senses.definition: a public statement that a person has committed a crime or a serious fault
senses.definitionCN: 公开指出某人犯了罪或有严重过失的话
senses.example: The accusation was read aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 那项指控在法庭上被大声宣读。
senses.why: The Latin causa means a lawsuit, so the noun began as the act of bringing a case rather than a private complaint.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 意为「诉讼」，所以这个名词最初指把案子提上法庭的行为，而不是私下的抱怨。

senses.title: The charge itself
senses.definition: the particular wrong that someone is said to have done
senses.definitionCN: 某人被说成做过的那件具体的错事
senses.example: The accusation against him was theft.
senses.exampleCN: 对他的指控是盗窃。
senses.why: Once a case is opened, the word shifts from the act of charging to the content of the charge, the thing written in the file.
senses.whyCN: 案子一立，词义就从「提出指控」转到「指控的内容」，也就是写进卷宗的那一条。

senses.title: An informal charge of blame
senses.definition: a claim of blame made outside any court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭之外提出的责备性说法
senses.example: Her accusation hurt him more than the fine.
senses.exampleCN: 她的指责比罚款更伤他。
senses.why: A lawsuit can shrink to a quarrel; the same pointing finger now appears at the dinner table rather than the dock.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼可以缩成一场争吵；同一根指点的手指，如今出现在餐桌边，而不是被告席前。

intro.en: The noun comes from the Latin verb for bringing a case, built on the word for a lawsuit.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语中「提起诉讼」的动词，其词根是「诉讼」。

items.en: causa meant a cause, a case or a lawsuit.
items.cn: causa 意为原因、案件或诉讼。

items.en: accusare meant to call someone to account before a court.
items.cn: accusare 意为在法庭上追究某人。

items.en: accusatio named the act of bringing such a charge.
items.cn: accusatio 指提出这种指控的行为。

items.en: the form passed through Old French before reaching English.
items.cn: 这个词形先经过古法语，再进入英语。

items.en: the noun now covers courts, news stories and family quarrels.
items.cn: 如今这个名词覆盖法庭、新闻与家庭争吵。

note.en: The first group is the accuse family; the second is other words for a charge.
note.cn: 第一组是 accuse 词族；第二组是别的表示指控的说法。

entries.definition: to say someone has done wrong
the person charged in a case
the person who makes a charge
showing that someone is blamed

a claim of wrongdoing not yet proved
responsibility for a fault
a formal accusation in law

normalIntro.en: The root causa, a lawsuit, is the same one inside cause.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 causa（诉讼）与 cause 里的那个词根是同一个。

normal.en: causa is a case or lawsuit, so accusation is born in court.
normal.cn: causa 是案件、诉讼，所以 accusation 出生在法庭。

normal.en: accuse is the verb underneath, and -ation names the act.
normal.cn: 底下的动词是 accuse，-ation 把它变成行为的名词。

normal.en: false accusation is the fixed phrase for a charge that is not true.
normal.cn: false accusation 是「不实指控」的固定说法。

normal.en: you deny or face an accusation, you do not usually answer one.
normal.cn: 常说的是 deny 或 face an accusation，一般不说 answer。

normal.en: the plural accusations often points to several separate claims.
normal.cn: 复数 accusations 常指分开的多项指控。

abstract.en: See a finger pointing straight across a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在法庭上直直指向对面。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with one charge written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸，上面只写了一项罪名。

abstract.en: Think of a sharp word at a dinner table that ends the meal.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌上的一句重话，让整顿饭就此结束。

examples.en: The company denied every accusation in the report.
examples.cn: 公司否认了报告中的每一项指控。

examples.en: A false accusation can ruin a good name.
examples.cn: 不实的指控能毁掉一个好名声。

examples.en: She met the accusation with silence rather than anger.
examples.cn: 面对指责，她用沉默而不是愤怒回应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿Q贼身」——阿Q被人指着说偷了东西，急得直跺脚。

root: 拉丁语 accusatio，源自 accusare（控告），词根 causa 意为「诉讼、案件」；本义是在法庭上提出追究，后泛指指控与指责。

sensesIntro.en: One pointing finger appears in three settings: the courtroom, the case file and the dinner table.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一根指点的手指出现在三处：法庭、卷宗与餐桌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointed and a name called out.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指一指，名字被点出。

branches.en: the public act of charging someone
branches.cn: 公开提出指控的行为

branches.en: the single offence written in the file
branches.cn: 卷宗里写明的那一项罪名

branches.en: blame spoken outside any court
branches.cn: 在法庭之外说出的责备

branches.en: the act and the content of a charge
branches.cn: 指控的行为与指控的内容

branches.en: a quarrel that borrows the language of law
branches.cn: 借用了法律语言的争吵

intro.en: A Latin prefix, the lawsuit root and a noun ending form the word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀、表示诉讼的词根和一个名词词尾，组成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: causa, lawsuit, also gives cause and the legal term causidicus.
latinIntro.cn: 表示诉讼的 causa 也给出 cause 以及法律术语 causidicus。

definition_zh: 指责的；非难的；控诉的；问罪式的
definition_en: suggesting that someone has done something wrong, or expressing an accusation
core_image: 皱起的眉头直指对方，像一根手指点在人身上
scene: 他翻出账本逐条核对，脸色越来越沉，抬头时满屋都静了。He gave her an accusatory look when the money was found missing.
sceneCN: 这里 accusatory 是「指责的、非难的」（第 1 个义项：用目光或语气暗示某人做错了事）；句意是发现钱不见了，他向她投去问罪的一瞥。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「指责地；非难地」
同根名词，义为「指控；指责」

senses.title: Blaming with looks or words

senses.exampleCN: 消色差双合透镜显著锐化了望远镜的成像。

normal.en: a- means without, chroma means colour: achromatic is colourless.
normal.cn: a- 表示「无」，chroma 表示「颜色」：achromatic 即无色。

normal.en: chromatic is the positive partner: with colour.
normal.cn: chromatic 是它的正面对照：有色的。

normal.en: monochromatic adds mono-, one: a single colour only.
normal.cn: monochromatic 再加 mono-（一）：只剩一种颜色。

normal.en: in optics an achromatic lens stops the rainbow fringing.
normal.cn: 光学里消色差透镜能止住彩虹色的边缘。

normal.en: photography calls plain black and white scenes achromatic.
normal.cn: 摄影里纯黑白画面被称为非彩色。

abstract.en: Picture a film where someone bleached every frame grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一部被逐帧漂成灰色的影片。

abstract.en: See a lens split light into a rainbow, then a second lens pulling the colours back together.
abstract.cn: 想象一片透镜把光拆成彩虹，另一片把颜色重新收拢。

abstract.en: Feel a room drained of hue, only outlines and shadows left.
abstract.cn: 体会一间被抽掉色相的房间，只剩轮廓与影子。

examples.en: Achromatic prints hung on the wall: only black, white and grey.
examples.cn: 墙上挂的是非彩色照片：只有黑、白与灰。

examples.en: The telescope improved sharply after the maker fitted an achromatic lens.
examples.cn: 装上消色差透镜后，望远镜的成像大幅改善。

examples.en: Patients with achromatic vision see the world as shades of grey.
examples.cn: 全色盲患者眼中的世界只有深浅不一的灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克罗马提克」——阿克把「罗」（彩色）都抹掉，画面只剩黑白灰。

root: 希腊语 achromatos（无色的）由否定前缀 a-（无）与 chroma（颜色）构成；十八世纪光学借科学拉丁语 achromaticus 造词，指消除色差的透镜。

sensesIntro.en: One act of removing colour serves three fields: plain vision, corrected optics, and unstained tissue.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「抽走颜色」的动作服务三个领域：纯粹的视觉、被校正的光学、以及不着色的组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: colour lifted out, leaving only light and dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：颜色被提起抽走，只剩明与暗。

branches.en: black, white and grey as the residue of colour removed
branches.cn: 颜色被移除后剩下的黑、白与灰

branches.en: lenses that pull every colour to one focus
branches.cn: 把各色光聚到同一焦点的透镜

branches.en: tissues that refuse the dye and stay pale
branches.cn: 拒绝染料、保持苍白的组织

branches.en: removing unwanted colour, whether in an image or in an error
branches.cn: 无论在图像还是误差里，都 unwanted 地移除颜色

branches.en: the neutral world left when hue is gone
branches.cn: 色相消失后剩下的中性世界

intro.en: A Greek negative, a colour root, and scientific endings build the family.
intro.cn: 希腊否定前缀、颜色词根与科学后缀构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: The colour root chroma is Greek, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: 颜色词根 chroma 出自希腊语，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 酸；酸性物质；酸性的；尖刻的
definition_en: a chemical substance that can dissolve metal, or something sour and sharp
core_image: 一滴酸液落在金属上，冒起细小的白泡
scene: 电池里的酸液沾到皮肤上会灼伤。The acid in the battery can burn your skin.
sceneCN: 这里的 acid 是「酸」（第 1 个义项：化学意义上的酸性物质）；句意是电池里的酸会灼伤皮肤。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「酸性的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「酸度」
由词干加动词后缀构成，义为「使变酸」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「尖刻地」

senses.title: A chemical that corrodes
senses.definition: a substance that reacts with metals and turns litmus red
senses.definitionCN: 能与金属反应、使石蕊变红的物质
senses.example: The lab stored the acid in a thick glass bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把这种酸存放在厚玻璃瓶里。
senses.why: Latin acidus meant sour, and the sour taste was the first test people had for this class of chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acidus 意为「酸的」，而酸味正是古人辨认这类化学物质的第一种检验方法。

senses.title: Sour or corrosive in quality
senses.definition: having a sour taste or the power to eat into a material
senses.definitionCN: 带有酸味，或具有腐蚀材料的能力
senses.example: Acid soil slows the growth of most vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 酸性土壤会拖慢多数蔬菜的生长。
senses.why: From the noun comes an adjective that describes anything sharing the sour, biting quality, whether soil, rain or fruit.
senses.whyCN: 从名词长出形容词，用来描述一切带酸、带咬劲的东西，无论是土壤、雨水还是果子。

senses.title: Biting in manner
senses.definition: sharp and unkind in speech or tone
senses.definitionCN: 言语或语气尖锐、不留情
senses.example: Her acid remark silenced the whole table.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖刻的一句话让满桌人都沉默了。
senses.why: A sour taste in the mouth becomes a sour tone in the voice, so the same adjective now describes a remark that burns.
senses.whyCN: 嘴里的酸味变成语气里的酸味，于是同一个形容词现在形容一句灼人的话。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin adjective for sour, from a root for sharp.
intro.cn: 这个词上溯到拉丁语中表示「酸」的形容词，其词根意为「尖锐」。

items.en: a reconstructed root meant sharp or pointed.
items.cn: 一个重构词根意为尖锐、带尖。

items.en: acere meant to be sour or sharp.
items.cn: acere 意为发酸、发尖。

items.en: acidus meant sour, and also sharp to the taste.
items.cn: acidus 意为酸的，也指味道尖利。

items.en: acid entered English first as an adjective and later as a noun.
items.cn: acid 先作形容词进入英语，后来才作名词。

items.en: chemistry gave the noun its precise sense, while the adjective kept the old bite.
items.cn: 化学给了名词精确含义，而形容词保留了旧日的尖刻。

note.en: The first group is the acid family; the second is other words for sourness and sharpness.
note.cn: 第一组是 acid 词族；第二组是别的表示酸与尖刻的词。

entries.definition: having the nature of an acid
the level of acid in something
to make or become acid
in a biting manner
having a sharp taste like lemon
sharply sour in a pleasant way
able to burn by chemical action, or bitterly sharp
having the opposite chemical nature

normalIntro.en: The root is Latin acere, to be sour, from a sharpness root.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 acere（发酸），更早来自表示「尖锐」的词根。

normal.en: acidus meant sour, and the sour taste named the chemical class.
normal.cn: acidus 意为酸，酸味给这一类化学物质命了名。

normal.en: acidic is the adjective for the chemical property, acidity the measure.
normal.cn: acidic 是化学性质的形容词，acidity 是度量。

normal.en: acid rain and acid soil are the common environmental phrases.
normal.cn: acid rain 与 acid soil 是常见的环境搭配。

normal.en: the acid test comes from using acid to check gold.
normal.cn: acid test 源自用酸检验黄金的做法。

normal.en: a sharp tongue is still called acid, keeping the old bite.
normal.cn: 尖刻的嘴仍被叫作 acid，保留了旧日的咬劲。

abstract.en: Watch a drop of acid bubble on a metal plate.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴酸落在金属板上冒起泡。

abstract.en: Bite into a lemon and feel your face tighten.
abstract.cn: 想象咬一口柠檬，整张脸都皱起来。

abstract.en: Hear one cutting remark end a cheerful conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象一句尖刻的话结束了一场热闹的谈话。

examples.en: Strong acid must be handled with thick gloves.
examples.cn: 强酸必须戴厚手套处理。

examples.en: The acid level in the lake rose after the spill.
examples.cn: 泄漏之后湖水酸度升高了。

examples.en: He answered the question in an acid tone.
examples.cn: 他用尖刻的语气回答了问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿酸的」——阿酸尝了一口青梅，酸得直吸气，嘴里还带点刺。

root: 拉丁语 acidus（酸的），源自 acere（发酸），更早可追到表示「尖锐」的印欧词根；本义是味道尖酸，后成为化学术语，并引申为言语尖刻。

sensesIntro.en: Sourness runs from the lab bottle to the soil to the human tongue.
sensesIntro.cn: 酸味从实验室的瓶子，走到土壤里，再走到人的舌头上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sour bite that leaves a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：酸得发咬，还留下痕迹。

branches.en: the chemical kept in a glass bottle
branches.cn: 装在玻璃瓶里的化学物质

branches.en: soil, rain or fruit with a sour quality
branches.cn: 带酸性的土壤、雨水或果子

branches.en: words that burn like acid
branches.cn: 像酸一样灼人的话

branches.en: the substance and the property it gives
branches.cn: 物质与它所赋予的性质

branches.en: a sour taste turning into a sour temper
branches.cn: 酸味变成酸脾气

intro.en: A Latin sour root plus adjective and noun endings make the word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「酸」词根加上形容词、名词词尾，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: acere, to be sour, is also behind acrid and vinegar's Latin name acetum.
latinIntro.cn: acere（发酸）也藏在 acrid 与醋的拉丁名 acetum 后面。

definition_zh: 酸化；使变酸；（土壤、水体）酸度升高
definition_en: to make or become acid, or to increase the acidity of something
core_image: 清水里滴进一滴酸，整杯水慢慢变酸
scene: 化工厂的废水排进湖里，湖边的老人皱起眉头。Years of pollution had acidified the lake water.
sceneCN: 这里 acidified 是「使酸化」（第 1 个义项：让物质酸性增强）；句意是多年的污染使湖水酸化了。

pos.zh: 酸化；使变酸；（使）酸度升高

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「酸化；酸化作用」
同根名词，义为「酸；酸性物质」
同根形容词，义为「酸的；酸性的」

senses.title: To turn something acid
senses.definition: to make a substance more acid, especially a liquid, soil, or water
senses.definitionCN: 使物质酸性增强，尤指液体、土壤或水体
senses.example: Adding vinegar acidified the marinade at once.
senses.exampleCN: 加入醋后腌汁立刻变酸了。
senses.why: Latin acidus means sour, and the -fy ending means to make; the verb is literally to make sour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acidus 意为「酸的」，词尾 -fy 表示「使成为」；这个动词的字面义就是「使变酸」。

senses.title: To become acid on its own
senses.definition: to become acid or more acidic, often gradually and by natural processes
senses.definitionCN: （自身）变为酸性或酸度渐增，常为渐进的自然过程
senses.example: Forest soils acidify slowly as fallen needles decompose.
senses.exampleCN: 随着松针腐烂，森林土壤慢慢酸化。
senses.why: The same making verb can point the other way: the substance does the making to itself as change creeps in.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「使成」动词也可以反向指向：变化悄悄发生时，物质在对自身施加这一过程。

senses.title: To treat with an acid in industry or chemistry
senses.definition: to add an acid to a material deliberately, as in processing or testing
senses.definitionCN: 有意向材料中加入酸，用于加工或检验
senses.example: The technician acidified the sample before running the test.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员在做检测前先对样本做了加酸处理。
senses.why: In the lab, making acid is a controlled step: the acid is a tool added on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，「使变酸」是一个受控步骤：酸是被有意加入的工具。

intro.en: A Latin word for sour meets a Latin ending that means to make.
intro.cn: 一个表示「酸」的拉丁词，遇上表示「使成为」的拉丁词尾。

items.en: *ak- is generally reconstructed as sharp or pointed, the feel of a sour taste.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ak- 表示「尖锐的」，正是酸味给人的感受。

items.en: acidus meant sour, and acidus acetum gave the family its sour core.
items.cn: 拉丁语 acidus 意为酸的，与醋一词同源，构成这个词族的「酸」核心。

items.en: acidare meant to make sour or to sour something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 acidare 意为使变酸。

items.en: scientific Latin acidificare remodelled the verb with facere, to make.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语 acidificare 用 facere（做）重塑了这个动词。

items.en: acidify entered technical English for chemistry, soil science, and industry.
items.cn: acidify 进入化学、土壤学与工业领域的英语用法。

note.en: The first group is the acid family; the second gathers other verbs of changing a property.
note.cn: 第一组是 acid 词族；第二组收集改变性质的其它动词。

entries.definition: a sour substance, or tasting sour
containing acid; acid-tasting
the level of acid in a substance
a flammable gas used in welding; it merely looks similar and comes from another root
entries.definitionCN: 乙炔（焊接用可燃气体）；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make or become sour in taste
to change chemically, often turning liquid sour
to make or become alkaline
to cancel out acidity with a base

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin sour root and the making ending.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆点围绕拉丁语「酸」词根与「使成」词尾。

normal.en: acidus is Latin for sour; acidify is to make sour.
normal.cn: acidus 是拉丁语的「酸」；acidify 就是使变酸。

normal.en: -fy means to make, as in purify and simplify.
normal.cn: -fy 表示「使成」，如 purify、simplify。

normal.en: acidification is the noun for the whole process.
normal.cn: acidification 是整个过程对应的名词。

normal.en: acid rain is the famous example of nature acidifying waters.
normal.cn: 酸雨是自然界酸化水体的著名例子。

normal.en: the opposite verb is alkalify, making things alkaline.
normal.cn: 反义动词是 alkalify，使变碱。

abstract.en: Watch a drop of lemon juice turn a glass of water sharp.
abstract.cn: 看着一滴柠檬汁让一杯水变得尖酸。

abstract.en: Picture needles falling year after year until the forest floor stings.
abstract.cn: 想象松针年年落下，直到林地的土壤发涩。

abstract.en: See a chemist tilt a bottle and watch the pH marker slide down.
abstract.cn: 想象化学家倾瓶加酸，看着 pH 标记滑落。

examples.en: Pollution from the plant acidified the stream within a decade.
examples.cn: 工厂排出的污染在十年间使溪流酸化。

examples.en: Gardeners add sulphur to acidify soil for blueberries.
examples.cn: 园丁加硫磺酸化土壤以种植蓝莓。

examples.en: The solution must be acidified before the colour test works.
examples.cn: 溶液必须先酸化，显色反应才能进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿西迪法爱」——阿西迪把法爱（醋）倒进水里，一整杯都酸了。

root: 拉丁语 acidus（酸的，一般认为源自原始印欧语 *ak-「尖锐的」）加 -fy（使成为）构成；本义是使物质变酸，后用于化学与土壤学的酸化过程。

sensesIntro.en: Making acid covers three directions: forcing a change, letting it creep in, and adding acid as a deliberate tool.
sensesIntro.cn: 「使变酸」涵盖三个方向：强行改变、任其渐变、以及有意加酸作为工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear liquid turning sharp drop by drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：清液一滴一滴变尖变酸。

branches.en: someone or something forces the sour change
branches.cn: 人或外力促成酸变

branches.en: nature drifts towards acidity without a hand
branches.cn: 无人干预时自然滑向酸性

branches.en: the lab adds acid as a deliberate step
branches.cn: 实验室有意加酸的步骤

branches.en: the same drift, fast or slow
branches.cn: 同一种酸化，或急或缓

branches.en: acidity rising until a test or a lake shows it
branches.cn: 酸度升高，直到检测或湖泊显现出来

intro.en: A sour Latin root and a making ending build the word; suffixes extend the family.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「酸」词根与「使成」词尾构成这个词；后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin acidus and its sour cousins vinegar and acetic share one root line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acidus 与醋、乙酸等表「酸」的词同属一条词源线。

definition_zh: 承认；确认收到；致谢；示意
definition_en: to accept that something is true, or to show that you have received or noticed something
core_image: 一个人举起手，表示「我看到了，也认了」
scene: 他没有辩解，立刻承认了自己的错误。He acknowledged the mistake at once.
sceneCN: 这里的 acknowledge 是「承认」（第 1 个义项：接受某事为真）；句意是他马上承认了错误。

pos.zh: 承认；确认收到；致谢；向……示意

collocations.zh: 向某人示意已注意到他

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「承认；致谢；回执」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「公认的」
加否定前缀构成，义为「未被承认的」

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept openly that a fact or a fault is real
senses.definitionCN: 公开接受某个事实或过失确实存在
senses.example: She acknowledged that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: The Old English base cnawan means to know, so to acknowledge is to let what you already know be known to others.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词基 cnawan 意为「知道」，所以 acknowledge 就是把自己已经知道的事也让别人知道。

senses.title: To confirm that something arrived
senses.definition: to tell someone formally that you have received a letter, parcel or message
senses.definitionCN: 正式告知对方，信、包裹或消息已经收到
senses.example: Please acknowledge receipt of this letter.
senses.exampleCN: 请确认收到此信。
senses.why: Knowing has a practical side: once the letter is in your hand, you say so, and the knowledge becomes a receipt.
senses.whyCN: 「知道」有实际的一面：信到了手里就说一声，这份知道便成了一张回执。

senses.title: To express thanks for help
senses.definition: to publicly thank a person or a group for their help
senses.definitionCN: 公开感谢某人或某群体提供的帮助
senses.example: The author acknowledged her editor in the preface.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在序言里感谢了编辑。
senses.why: To acknowledge a debt is to admit you owe it; in print the same verb becomes a formal thank-you.
senses.whyCN: 承认欠人情，就是承认这笔账存在；写进书里，同一个动词就成了一封正式的谢辞。

senses.title: To show that you have noticed someone
senses.definition: to greet a person with a nod, a smile or a few words
senses.definitionCN: 用点头、微笑或几句话向人致意
senses.example: He acknowledged me with a brief nod.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻轻点了一下头，算是跟我打了招呼。
senses.why: The smallest form of admitting a fact is admitting a person is there; a nod says I know you without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 承认事实最小的形式，就是承认某人在场；一个点头表示「我看见你了」，却不必停下脚步。

intro.en: The word is native English in its core, with a suffix added in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 这个词的核心是英语本土的，中世纪时又加了一个后缀。

items.en: oncnawan meant to understand or to recognize.
items.cn: oncnawan 意为理解或认出。

items.en: the verb became aknowen, to know and to admit.
items.cn: 这个动词演变为 aknowen，意为知道并承认。

items.en: the ending -ledge was added, giving the modern spelling acknowledge.
items.cn: 词尾 -ledge 被加上去，形成现代拼写 acknowledge。

items.en: the noun acknowledgement appeared for the act of admitting or thanking.
items.cn: 名词 acknowledgement 出现，指承认或致谢的行为。

items.en: the verb now covers emails, applause and a passing nod.
items.cn: 如今这个动词涵盖邮件回执、致谢以及擦肩而过的一个点头。

note.en: The first group is the acknowledge family; the second is other verbs of admitting.
note.cn: 第一组是 acknowledge 词族；第二组是别的表示承认的动词。

intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀和一个「知道」词根构成这个动词，再经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: cognoscere, to know, also gives recognize, cognition and notice.
latinIntro.cn: cognoscere（知道）也给出 recognize、cognition 与 notice。

definition_en: unwilling acceptance of something without protest, or silent agreement by not objecting
core_image: 皱着眉却闭上了嘴，不再反对
scene: 委员会提出改期，他心里不满，却只是点了点头。He nodded in acquiescence when the board announced the delay.
sceneCN: 这里 acquiescence 是「默许」（第 1 个义项：不作抗议地接受）；句意是董事会宣布延期时，他点头默许。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「默许；勉强同意」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「默认的；顺从的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「默认地；顺从地」

senses.title: Silent acceptance
senses.definition: acceptance of a decision or situation without protest, though often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 对决定或局面不作抗议地接受，常出于无奈
senses.example: Her silence was taken as acquiescence in the new schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默被当作对新时间表的默许。
senses.why: Latin quies means rest; to acquiesce is to sit down into the situation and stop resisting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quies 意为「安歇」；acquiesce 就是坐进这个局面、停止抵抗。

senses.title: Compliance under pressure
senses.definition: compliance that comes from yielding to pressure or authority rather than genuine agreement
senses.definitionCN: 因迫于压力或权威而顺从，并非真心赞同
senses.example: The workers signed the new rules in reluctant acquiescence.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们勉强顺从地签下了新规章。
senses.why: Rest can be forced: the body stills because fighting seems useless, not because the heart agrees.
senses.whyCN: 安歇也可以是被逼出来的：身体安静下来是因为抗不过，而不是心服。

intro.en: A Latin verb of resting quietly becomes a noun of silent consent.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「安静歇息」的动词化为「默许」的名词。

items.en: *kweh- is generally reconstructed as to rest or be quiet; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *kweh- 表示「歇息、安静」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: quies meant rest, quiet, the stillness of things settled.
items.cn: 拉丁语 quies 意为安歇、安静，指安定下来的静止。

items.en: acquiescere joined ad-, towards, with quiescere, to settle into rest.
items.cn: acquiescere 由 ad-（朝向）与 quiescere（入于安歇）结合。

items.en: acquiesce entered English in legal and political writing for yielding consent.
items.cn: 十七世纪 acquiesce 进入英语的法律与政论文体，表示让步性的同意。

items.en: acquiescence now names the quiet nod that follows disagreement.
items.cn: 如今 acquiescence 专指异议之后的安静点头。

note.en: The first group is the quies family; the second gathers words for consent with different warmth.
note.cn: 第一组是 quies 词族；第二组收集温度各异的「同意」。

entries.definition: to accept without protest
tending to accept without protest
still and silent, from the same Latin rest root
a person one knows slightly; it merely looks similar and comes from another root
entries.definitionCN: 熟人；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: genuine agreement, often formal
acting in accordance with rules or demands
yielding to a stronger power
formal agreement to a proposal

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin rest root and the nod that ends resistance.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆点围绕拉丁语「安歇」词根与结束抵抗的点头。

normal.en: quies is Latin for rest; acquiescence is resting into a decision.
normal.cn: quies 是拉丁语的「安歇」；acquiescence 就是坐进决定里不再争。

normal.en: ad- plus quiescere: to settle towards quiet.
normal.cn: ad- 加 quiescere：趋向安歇。

normal.en: acquiesce is the verb, acquiescent the adjective, acquiescence the noun.
normal.cn: acquiesce 是动词，acquiescent 是形容词，acquiescence 是名词。

normal.en: tacit acquiescence means agreement by silence.
normal.cn: tacit acquiescence 指以沉默达成的默认。

normal.en: quiet shares the same Latin rest root.
normal.cn: quiet 与之同出拉丁「安歇」词根。

abstract.en: Picture a fist unclenching on the meeting table.
abstract.cn: 想象会议桌上缓缓松开的拳头。

abstract.en: Feel the sigh before the reluctant yes.
abstract.cn: 体会那句勉强的「好」之前的一声叹息。

abstract.en: See a chair being sat in slowly, protest folding away.
abstract.cn: 想象人慢慢坐进椅子，抗议被叠起收走。

examples.en: His acquiescence did not mean approval; he simply stopped arguing.
examples.cn: 他的默许并不代表赞成，只是不再争辩。

examples.en: The treaty was passed with the quiet acquiescence of all parties.
examples.cn: 条约在各方默默默许下获得通过。

examples.en: She nodded in acquiescence and turned back to her desk.
examples.cn: 她点头默许，转身回到书桌前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奎爱森斯」——阿奎心里不乐意，却爱森森（安安静静）点头了。

root: 拉丁语 acquiescere（入于安歇）由 ad-（朝向）与 quiescere（歇息）构成，quies 意为安静；本义是安顿下来不再反抗，后引申为默许与勉强顺从。

sensesIntro.en: Two yields grow from one rest: the silent nod of acceptance and the reluctant bow to pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「安歇」长出两种让步：默默的点头，与迫于压力的低头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist relaxing into an open, silent hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：拳头松开，化作一只安静的摊开的手。

branches.en: protest stops and silence counts as consent
branches.cn: 抗议停止，沉默即算同意

branches.en: authority presses and the body yields
branches.cn: 权威施压，身体退让

branches.en: resting into a decision one did not choose
branches.cn: 安顿进一个并非自己选定的决定

branches.en: the distance between yielding and agreeing
branches.cn: 顺从与赞同之间的距离

branches.en: the nod, the sigh, the quiet signature
branches.cn: 点头、叹息与安静的签字

intro.en: A Latin prefix and a rest root build the word; endings make the verb, adjective, and noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁前缀与「安歇」词根构成全词；词尾派生出动词、形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin quies and quiescere are recorded ancestors of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quies 与 quiescere 是整个词族有据可查的祖先。

latinEntries.meaning: to settle into rest, to accept

definition_en: to get something, often through effort, purchase or experience
core_image: 一只手把一件原本不属于自己的东西收进怀里
scene: 去年她买下了街角那家小书店。She acquired a small bookshop last year.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquire 是「收购」（第 3 个义项：买下企业或资产）；句意是去年她收购了一家小书店。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「收购；获得；习得」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「收购方」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「贪得的」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: To obtain an object or property
senses.definition: to come to own something that you did not have before
senses.definitionCN: 得到原本不属于自己的东西，成为它的主人
senses.example: He acquired a rare stamp at the auction.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拍卖会上得到一枚珍稀邮票。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to seek in addition, so the first sense is simply the end of a search: the thing is now yours.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「额外去寻求」，所以第一个义项就是寻求的终点：东西归你了。

senses.title: To learn a skill or body of knowledge
senses.definition: to come to have a skill or understanding through practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过练习逐渐拥有某种技能或理解
senses.example: Children acquire language without formal lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童不用正式上课就能习得语言。
senses.why: What is true of objects is true of abilities: they can be gained over time, so the verb moves from possessions to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 东西如此，能力也如此：它们可以随时间获得，于是这个动词从财物挪到了头脑。

senses.title: To buy up a company
senses.definition: to take control of a business by buying it
senses.definitionCN: 通过购买取得一家企业的控制权
senses.example: The group acquired three smaller rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团收购了三家较小的竞争对手。
senses.why: In business the object grows large, but the grammar stays the same: one owner is replaced by another through a purchase.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里宾语变大了，语法却没变：通过一笔买卖，一个主人换成了另一个主人。

senses.title: To come to have a habit or name
senses.definition: to develop a habit, a taste or a reputation over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间形成习惯、口味或名声
senses.example: The town acquired a reputation for good bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇子渐渐以好面包闻名。
senses.why: Reputation and habits are not bought, yet they are still gained; the verb treats them as things that settle on a person.
senses.whyCN: 名声与习惯不是买来的，却仍然是「得来」的；这个动词把它们当作落在人身上的东西。

intro.en: The word is Latin for seeking something in addition, built from a prefix and a verb of searching.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语中意为「额外去寻求」，由一个前缀和一个表示寻找的动词构成。

items.en: quaerere meant to seek, to ask or to try to get.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找、询问或设法取得。

items.en: acquirere added ad-, towards, to the same search.
items.cn: acquirere 在同一个「寻找」前加了表示朝向的 ad-。

items.en: the past participle acquisitus described what had been gained.
items.cn: 过去分词 acquisitus 形容已经取得的东西。

items.en: acquire entered English as a verb of obtaining.
items.cn: acquire 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示获得的动词。

items.en: it now covers property, skills, habits and corporate takeovers.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖财产、技能、习惯与企业收购。

note.en: The first group is the acquisition family; the second is other verbs of getting.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquisition 词族；第二组是别的表示获得的动词。

normalIntro.en: The Latin search verb quaerere is the root, also seen in inquire and require.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「寻找」动词 quaerere 是词根，inquire 与 require 里也能看到它。

normal.en: quaerere means to seek, so acquire is to end a search with a gain.
normal.cn: quaerere 意为寻找，所以 acquire 是带着收获结束寻找。

normal.en: acquisition is the noun, acquirer the buyer.
normal.cn: 名词是 acquisition，收购方是 acquirer。

normal.en: acquire knowledge and acquire skills are the learning pair.
normal.cn: acquire knowledge 与 acquire skills 是学习类的一对搭配。

normal.en: acquire a taste for means to grow to like something.
normal.cn: acquire a taste for 意为渐渐喜欢上某物。

normal.en: in business, acquire a company means to buy control of it.
normal.cn: 在商业里，acquire a company 意为买下它的控制权。

abstract.en: See a hand close around an object that was not there before.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手合拢，把原先不在手里的东西握住。

abstract.en: Picture a child picking up a new word each day.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子每天捡起一个新词。

abstract.en: Think of a shop sign being lowered and another raised above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块招牌被摘下，另一块挂了上去。

examples.en: She acquired the painting for a modest sum.
examples.cn: 她花不多的钱得到了那幅画。

examples.en: Students acquire reading skills through daily practice.
examples.cn: 学生通过每日练习习得阅读技能。

examples.en: The chain acquired two local bakeries this spring.
examples.cn: 这家连锁店今年春天收购了两家本地面包房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿快尔」——阿快眼疾手快，一把将看中的东西搂进怀里。

root: 拉丁语 acquirere（求得），由 ad-（朝向）与 quaerere（寻找、求取）构成；本义是「寻求而得到」，后引申为习得、养成与收购。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of getting covers things, skills, companies and reputations.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「得到」的动词，管着东西、技能、公司与名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on what it has sought.
core.cn: 核心意象：寻到手边，手合拢。

branches.en: a stamp or a painting now owned
branches.cn: 归到名下的邮票或画作

branches.en: a language or a skill learned by practice
branches.cn: 练出来的语言或技能

branches.en: a rival firm bought for control
branches.cn: 为取得控制权而买下的对手

branches.en: a habit or a name that settles on someone
branches.cn: 落在某人身上的习惯或名声

branches.en: small purchases and large takeovers share one verb
branches.cn: 小额购入与大型收购共用一个动词

intro.en: A Latin prefix and a verb of seeking build the word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀和一个表示寻找的动词，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: quaerere, to seek, also underlies inquire, require and question.
latinIntro.cn: quaerere（寻找）也是 inquire、require 与 question 的底子。

definition_en: the act of gaining something, especially the buying of a company or the learning of a skill
core_image: 一份合同签完，另一家公司的招牌被换下来
scene: 收购那家对手公司，前后花了好几个月。The acquisition of the rival firm took months.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquisition 是「收购」（第 1 个义项：买下企业）；句意是收购对手公司花了几个月。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「获得；收购」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「收购方」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「贪得的」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: The buying of a company
senses.definition: the purchase of one business by another
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业买下另一家企业
senses.example: The acquisition added three factories to the group.
senses.exampleCN: 这次收购为集团增加了三家工厂。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of gaining into a business event, and in finance the most visible gain is a bought rival.
senses.whyCN: 名词把「取得」变成一个商业事件，而在金融里最显眼的取得，就是买下一家对手。

senses.title: The gaining of knowledge or skill
senses.definition: the process of coming to have information or an ability
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐拥有知识或能力的过程
senses.example: The acquisition of a new language takes years.
senses.exampleCN: 掌握一门新语言需要多年。
senses.why: What is bought in business is learned in the mind, so the same noun names the slow gaining of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 商业里用钱买的东西，在头脑里靠学得来，于是同一个名词也指技能缓慢到手的过程。

senses.title: Something newly obtained
senses.definition: an object that has recently been gained, especially by a museum
senses.definitionCN: 最近得到的东西，尤指博物馆的新藏品
senses.example: The painting is the museum's latest acquisition.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画是博物馆最新入藏的藏品。
senses.why: From the act comes the object: once the deal closes, the thing bought stands in the room and is called an acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 从行为落到物件：交易一完成，买来的东西就摆在屋里，被称作一件 acquisition。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun of the verb for seeking and gaining.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语中「寻求并获得」动词的动作名词。

items.en: acquirere meant to gain by seeking.

items.en: acquisitio named the act of gaining.
items.cn: acquisitio 指取得的行为。

items.en: acquisition entered English as a noun of obtaining.
items.cn: acquisition 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示获得的名词。

items.en: finance gave it the dominant sense of buying a company.
items.cn: 金融赋予了它「买下公司」这一主要含义。

note.en: The first group is the acquire family; the second is other words for a purchase or gain.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquire 词族；第二组是别的表示购买或获得的词。

normal.en: a museum calls each new piece its latest acquisition.
normal.cn: 博物馆把每件新入藏的东西称作最新藏品。

normal.en: the plural acquisitions can mean several deals or several objects.
normal.cn: 复数 acquisitions 既可指多笔交易，也可指多件藏品。

abstract.en: See a sign being unscrewed and another lifted into place.
abstract.cn: 想象旧招牌被拧下来，新招牌被吊上去。

abstract.en: Picture a child adding one new word a day.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子每天增加一个新词。

abstract.en: Think of a glass case holding a newly bought painting.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜里放着一幅刚买来的画。

examples.en: Reading widely speeds the acquisition of vocabulary.
examples.cn: 广泛阅读能加快词汇的习得。

examples.en: The sculpture is the gallery's most valuable acquisition.
examples.cn: 这座雕像是画廊最珍贵的藏品。

branches.cn: 学习与购买共享同一种求得的动力

definition_zh: 宣判无罪；开释；（ oneself）表现得体
definition_en: to formally decide in court that someone is not guilty, or to behave in a stated way
core_image: 法官落槌：指控被放下，被告自由离席
scene: 证人作证完毕，陪审团低声商议了许久。The jury acquitted the defendant after three days of deliberation.
sceneCN: 这里 acquitted 是「宣判无罪」（第 1 个义项：法庭正式裁定无罪）；句意是陪审团经三天评议宣告被告无罪。

pos.zh: （与 oneself 连用）表现得；履行

collocations.zh: 宣判某人某项罪名不成立

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「无罪判决；开释」
法律术语，义为「（陪审团的）无罪裁定」

senses.title: To declare not guilty
senses.definition: of a court or jury, to decide formally that a person on trial is not guilty
senses.definitionCN: 法庭或陪审团正式裁定受审者无罪
senses.example: The court acquitted him for lack of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院因证据不足判他无罪。
senses.why: Latin quire meant to pay a debt; acquit began as paying off or settling a charge, which grew into clearing it away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quire 意为「偿清」；acquit 起初指清偿了结一笔债务或指控，后来引申为洗清罪名。

senses.title: To free from a duty or debt
senses.definition: to release someone from a responsibility, duty, or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 使人卸除责任、义务或债务
senses.example: A final payment acquitted the company of its debt.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一笔付款使公司卸清了债务。

definition_en: an area of land measured in acres, or the total number of acres

senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了河谷里每座葡萄园的英亩数。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the sharp root and the sting it gives to smoke and speech.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆点围绕「尖锐」词根，以及它赋予烟与言语的刺感。

normal.en: acer is Latin for sharp; acrid is sharpness you smell.
normal.cn: acer 是拉丁语的「尖锐」；acrid 是用鼻子感到的尖锐。

normal.en: acid and acrid are cousins: sour taste, stinging smell.
normal.cn: acid 与 acrid 是近亲：一个酸舌头，一个呛鼻子。

normal.en: acrimony keeps the root for bitter tempers.
normal.cn: acrimony 把词根留给了刻毒的脾气。

normal.en: eager also carries the keen sense of acer.
normal.cn: eager 同样带着 acer「热切」的含义。

normal.en: the word pairs naturally with smoke, fumes and remarks.
normal.cn: 这个词常与 smoke、fumes、remarks 搭配。

abstract.en: Breathe in near a burnt pan and feel the nose prickle.
abstract.cn: 凑近烧糊的锅吸气，体会鼻腔的刺痒。

abstract.en: Hear a reply land like vinegar on a wound.
abstract.cn: 听一句回答像醋泼在伤口上。

abstract.en: See grey smoke curling from a scorched cable.
abstract.cn: 想象灰烟从烧焦的电缆上盘旋而起。

examples.en: Acrid smoke forced the family out of the burning house.
examples.cn: 刺鼻的浓烟迫使一家人撤离起火的房子。

examples.en: The debate grew acrid as the candidates traded barbs.
examples.cn: 候选人互相讥讽，辩论变得火药味十足。

examples.en: An acrid tang of ammonia rose from the cleaning bucket.
examples.cn: 清洁桶里泛起刺鼻的氨水味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克瑞德」——阿克被瑞德呛得直咳：这味儿太刺鼻。

root: 拉丁语 acer（尖锐的）经科学拉丁语 acridus 进入英语，与 acidus（酸的）同出原始印欧语 *ak-（一般认为表「尖锐」）；本义是气味与味道的刺激感，后引申为言语刻毒。

sensesIntro.en: One sting serves nose and temper alike: chemical fumes in the air, barbed words in the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种刺感既属于鼻子也属于脾气：空气里的化学烟雾，空气里带钩的话语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: smoke that makes eyes water and voices that make tempers burn.
core.cn: 核心意象：熏得人流泪的烟，与让人发火的言语。

branches.en: fumes and tastes that prick the senses
branches.cn: 刺痛感官的烟雾与味道

branches.en: remarks that prick like fumes
branches.cn: 如烟雾般刺人的言语

branches.en: the shared sting of chemistry and character
branches.cn: 化学品与性格共用的刺感

branches.en: air that burns, whether from fire or from speech
branches.cn: 无论是火还是话，都会灼人的空气

branches.en: the smell that empties a room
branches.cn: 把人赶出房间的气味

intro.en: A sharp Latin root and soft English endings build the word.
intro.cn: 拉丁「尖锐」词根与英语词尾构成全词。

latinIntro.en: Latin acer, acidus and acrimonia share one Indo-European sharp root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acer、acidus 与 acrimonia 同属一个印欧「尖锐」词根。
